title: Democracy's Workplaces in the Agora
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: A schematic plan of the Ancient Agora of Athens with ten clickable places and nine job cards of Athenian public life; the learner selects where each job was done, and a numbered badge is pinned beside the correct building.

educational.topic: The buildings of the Ancient Agora of Athens and the work of Athenian democracy
learningObjectives: Classify nine jobs of Athenian public life by the Agora building or monument where each was done, choosing correctly for at least 7 of 9 on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification on a schematic plan with one scored attempt per card, immediate feedback, and pinned badges
keyQuestions: Where in the Agora would you go to do this job?
Why did a charge of impiety start at a stoa rather than a court?
Which side of the square held most of the democracy's offices?
commonMisconceptions: The Agora was only a market.
Trials started in a courtroom, when charges of impiety were filed with the King Archon at the Royal Stoa.
Philosophy was taught in schools with buildings, when the Stoics met in a public stoa.
The Stoa of Attalos dates from Socrates' time, when it was built about 250 years later.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on nine job cards (mastery: 7 of 9, with card 5 correct).
Explain why the charge against Socrates was filed at the Royal Stoa.
